input.prompt:
In the repo /tmp/task-records-spruce/source, read registry/model.py (404 lines) in full, and registry/providers/github.py (536 lines) sections relevant to metadata handling.

I need a precise map of the metadata-block parsing/writing flow, because there's a bug: when task text (e.g. a GitHub issue body, or a task description quoted in some doc) contains an *unfinished* example metadata block (one with METADATA_BEGIN `<!-- task-registry:begin -->` but no matching METADATA_END `<!-- task-registry:end -->`, or a trailing unfinished block after a real complete one) BEFORE or AFTER the real complete block, the parser can pick up fields from the wrong (incomplete/example) block instead of the real, complete one. This can invent a bogus parent or dependency, and can interfere with task identity (task-id field).

Please answer with structured bullets, quoting file:line anchors, covering:

1. The exact definitions of `METADATA_BEGIN` and `METADATA_END` in model.py, and the full source of `parse_metadata_block(body)` — quote it verbatim with line numbers. Explain exactly how it locates the block currently (does it use the FIRST occurrence of METADATA_BEGIN and the first following METADATA_END? What happens if there are multiple `<!-- task-registry:begin -->` markers, or a begin with no matching end?).

2. The full source of `render_metadata_block(task)` (the writer) — quote it verbatim with line numbers. What fields does it emit and in what format (task-id, kind, parent, depends-on, spec, source, evidence, etc.)? Does it always emit a complete begin...end pair?

3. The full source of whatever function locates the block's *position* for rewriting purposes (looks like there's a helper around model.py:306-314 that finds start/end positions, possibly called `_find_metadata_block` or similar) — quote it verbatim. Does IT correctly skip incomplete/nested begin markers, or does it have the same bug as parse_metadata_block, or does it behave differently (which would itself indicate a reader/writer disagreement)?

4. The full source of `upsert_metadata_block(body, task)` and `task_from_metadata(...)` (used by github.py) — quote verbatim with line numbers. How does upsert_metadata_block use the position-finding helper vs parse_metadata_block? Do reader and writer agree on which block is "the" block when there are multiple candidate begin/end marker pairs in body text (e.g. one incomplete, one complete)?

5. Every call site of `parse_metadata_block`, `render_metadata_block`, `upsert_metadata_block`, `task_from_metadata`, `METADATA_BEGIN`, `METADATA_END` across the whole registry/ directory (both in model.py itself and in providers/local.py, providers/github.py, and anywhere else) — file:line for each, with 1-line description of how each call site uses the result (e.g. "local.py:156 parses metadata read from disk to build a Task").

6. In github.py, quote the surrounding context (roughly 20 lines before/after) of the `task_from_metadata` call at github.py:256 and the `upsert_metadata_block` call at github.py:338, so I can see exactly what body text is passed in (issue body from GitHub API, human-editable) and how the resulting Task fields (especially `id`, `parent`, `depends_on`) are used afterward.

7. Any existing tests for parse_metadata_block / render_metadata_block / upsert_metadata_block / task_from_metadata — search the whole repo for a tests/ directory or test_*.py files, list every test function name that touches metadata parsing, and quote any test that constructs a body string with more than one `<!-- task-registry:begin -->`/`<!-- task-registry:end -->` occurrence (multiple blocks, or an unfinished block).

Do not propose any fix or edit. Do not reason about correctness or architecture — just report facts with file:line anchors so I can implement the fix myself.

The bug: task descriptions/issue bodies can quote an *earlier, unfinished* example metadata block (e.g. in a bug report showing "here's what an incomplete block looks like") BEFORE the actual, complete, real metadata block later in the same text. The parser (and/or the writer) may pick fields from the wrong (quoted/incomplete) block instead of the real complete one, which can invent a bogus `parent` or `depends-on` field, or otherwise corrupt task identity. There's also a case of a trailing *unfinished* example block appearing *after* the real block, which must not interfere either.

Please read (in bounded chunks, respecting the 350-line read gate) and report on:

1. registry/model.py: the exact definitions of `METADATA_BEGIN`, `METADATA_END`, `parse_metadata_block`, `render_metadata_block`, `section`, and any related helpers (e.g. how it finds the block boundaries — regex vs string search, first-match vs last-match, whether it validates the block is "complete", how depends-on/parent/evidence lists are parsed, whether commas inside prose values are handled). Give exact file:line ranges and the literal logic (loop/regex) used to locate the block.
2. registry/providers/local.py: how `parse_metadata_block` and `render_metadata_block` are called (I already know this file: `_read`, `_render`, `_merged_with_existing`, `_unmanaged_regions` around lines 128-280). Note anything relevant about multiple blocks in one file (in `_unmanaged_regions`, note the `in_metadata` state machine at lines ~266-280 - does it handle multiple METADATA_BEGIN/END pairs, or nested/repeated markers, correctly?).
3. registry/providers/github.py: search for any usage of `parse_metadata_block`, `render_metadata_block`, `METADATA_BEGIN`, `METADATA_END`, or manual metadata-block extraction from GitHub issue/PR body text. GitHub issue bodies are untrusted user text that could contain quoted examples of the block syntax. Report exact file:line and logic for how it finds "the" block in an issue body (first occurrence? last occurrence? only complete blocks?).
4. registry/index.py and registry/config.py: search (grep first) for `parse_metadata_block`, `render_metadata_block`, `METADATA_BEGIN`, `METADATA_END` — report any hits with file:line and surrounding logic. If no hits, just say so.
5. Any existing tests (search the whole repo for test files, e.g. `test_*.py` or `*_test.py` or a `tests/` directory) that cover `parse_metadata_block` — report file:line of relevant test functions and what scenarios they currently cover (especially multiple blocks, incomplete blocks, quoted examples).

For each function/consumer, tell me:
- Exact source anchors (file:line)
- What "complete block" vs "incomplete block" means in the current code (is there any validation at all, or does it just find first BEGIN...END pair naively?)
- Whether the writer (render_metadata_block / _render in local.py) and reader (parse_metadata_block) agree on which block is authoritative when multiple candidate blocks exist in one text
- Any unresolved questions/ambiguities you could not settle by reading

This is a research/mapping task only — do not propose a fix or edit any files. Just give me the structured map with source anchors.
